chunks: Fadalah ibn Nizar narrated from al-Husayn ibn Abdullah who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'One who refrains from [impugning] the honor of people, Allah will pardon him [and protect his reputation] on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever restrains his anger from the people, Allah will restrain His anger from him on the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.أَعْرَاضِ: Honor, dignity, or reputation of people
key_terms.أَقَالَهُ: He pardoned him / He excused him

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of controlling one's anger and guarding people's honor according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far al-Hasan al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a reciprocal divine justice where guarding one's tongue from backbiting and controlling one's temper are met with Allah's pardon and restraint of His wrath. This hadith, found in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, underscores the spiritual discipline of *kaff al-lisan* (restraining the tongue) as a means to achieve inner peace and divine favor on the Day of Resurrection.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: Faḍālah ibn Nizāz [1] narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbdillāh who said, “Abū Jaʿfar [al-Bāqir] (a) said, ‘One who refrains from [impugning] the honor of people, Allah will pardon him [and protect his reputation] onthe Day of Resurrection, and whoever restrains his anger from the people, Allah will restrain His anger from him on the Day of Resurrection.’”
